drip.author: streetcar_named_delay
drip.title: A class trip got on my streetcar holding a walking rope, and by the third stop the teacher had counted one extra kid
drip.body:
About twenty grade twos got on at Parliament, each hanging onto a loop of one of those walking ropes. The car was packed. When it lurched, a man in a suit reached for the pole, missed, and caught a loop on the rope instead.

The teacher counted heads at every stop. At the third one she got one extra. The whole car went silent while she followed the rope with her eyes, loop by loop, all the way up to his tie. He looked down, said "oh," and did not let go, because the car was still moving and he had made his choice.

comments.author: parallel_parker
comments.body: please tell me he got off with them. I need to know how far he took the commitment

replies.author: streetcar_named_delay
replies.body: He let go at St. Andrew, handed the loop back to the teacher with a small nod like he was returning a library book, and walked into the subway. A professional to the end.

comments.author: SaveStateSteve
comments.body: he joined the party mid-quest and nobody had the heart to kick him out

comments.author: half_marathon_harold
comments.body: honestly the walking rope is an elite system. I'd join a running club that used one. nobody gets dropped on the hills

comments.author: left_on_red
comments.body: This is the most anyone on that line has held onto anything in years, and I'm including the schedule.

comments.author: codfather
comments.body: safest that man's been on public transit in his life, b'y. twenty youngsters and a teacher watching his back

drip.author: half_marathon_harold
drip.title: My 'lay out the running kit the night before' system has one flaw: night-before me still thinks it's August
drip.body:
Got up in the dark and put on the pile without thinking, exactly as designed. Shorts. Singlet. Out the door. It was three degrees.

A man scraping frost off his windshield looked up and said "bold" in the tone doctors use for "interesting." I ran the full 12 km anyway, because turning back would mean evening me wins, and evening me did this to us.

comments.author: gluten_full
comments.body: evening you is a menace, and I say that as someone who once set a 4 a.m. alarm to feed a jar

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: we have a guy who shows up to shinny in shorts until the outdoor rinks freeze. we've stopped asking whether it's toughness or a laundry situation

comments.author: prairiedialup
comments.body: three degrees in shorts is just september in saskatchewan. the frost guy was being polite

replies.author: half_marathon_harold
replies.body: he had gloves. he had a scraper. he had every right to judge

comments.author: FocalPointFran
comments.body: I use that exact doctor-voice "bold" on every groom who insists he won't need a jacket for October portraits.

comments.author: petty_officer_mittens
comments.body: the large human in my care also dresses based on yesterday. this is why i wear the same coat every day of the year. it is always correct

drip.author: codfather
drip.title: Went to tarp the woodpile for the winter. The wind had other plans for the tarp, and briefly for me.
drip.body:
Got two corners down. Wind got the other two. Next thing I'm skiing across the yard in me rubber boots hanging onto it like a kite. Neighbour leans over the fence with his tea and says "you want a hand with that, my son?" I says no b'y, I'm grand.

Let go at the property line out of pride. Last seen heading east. If anyone in Ireland finds a blue tarp, she's yours now. Woodpile's still out there, naked as the day it was split.

comments.author: prairiedialup
comments.body: every farmer out here has lost a tarp to the wind and every single one of them let go at the property line. nobody taught us that. we just know

comments.author: streetcar_named_delay
comments.body: "You want a hand?" "No, I'm grand." The entire third act is two men declining to help each other with tremendous warmth.

comments.author: stormglass
comments.body: Nova Scotia checking in. Ours don't blow away, they just relocate into the neighbour's tree and everyone agrees to wait for spring.

replies.author: codfather
replies.body: the tree tarp. a maritime heirloom. some of them have been up there longer than the tree

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: letting go at the property line is textbook. you never chase it into the other team's zone

comments.author: parallel_parker
comments.body: real hero here is the neighbour. offered once, respected the answer, and got to watch the whole thing with a hot tea. that's a man who knows how to have an evening

drip.author: FocalPointFran
drip.title: Orchard wedding yesterday. A wasp landed on the officiant's nose right at 'you may now kiss the bride.'
drip.body:
He did not flinch. He finished the sentence. The couple kissed. Then he said "excuse me" very calmly and walked into the apple trees at a pace I can only describe as brisk.

Everyone waited. He came back a minute later, straightened his notes, and said "where were we." The best frame of the day is the kiss in the foreground with a man speed-walking into the Cortlands behind them. It's the album cover. They didn't even hesitate.

comments.author: half_marathon_harold
comments.body: brisk pace into the orchard. I know that stride. that's a man who has been chased before

comments.author: prairiedialup
comments.body: september wasps are just summer wasps who've stopped pretending to be polite

replies.author: FocalPointFran
replies.body: Orchard weddings this time of year come with a wasp clause now. It's in my contract right under drunk uncles.

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: finished the sentence first. that's playing through to the whistle

comments.author: petty_officer_mittens
comments.body: the wasp was not an intruder. the wasp was a guest who ignored the dress code. it wore stripes. to a wedding

comments.author: gluten_full
comments.body: "where were we" is the most composed thing a human being has ever said. I would like him to officiate the rest of my life

drip.author: gluten_full
drip.title: Put my sourdough starter in the oven with the light on to keep her warm now that the kitchen's cold. Then I preheated the oven.
drip.body:
Gertrude has been having a hard time since the kitchen started dropping to about 18 degrees overnight, so I've been tucking her in the oven with only the light on. Little sauna. Very cozy. Very clever of me.

This morning I preheated for muffins. Noticed about four minutes in, when the kitchen started to smell like a bakery that had made a mistake. The lid of her jar has warped into a shape I can only describe as surprised. Gertrude herself is alive, sulking, and bubbling again already, which I believe is out of spite.

comments.author: prairiedialup
comments.body: that's not a starter anymore. that's a finisher

comments.author: SaveStateSteve
comments.body: she took fall damage and respawned at the last checkpoint. she's a speedrunner now

comments.author: brine_shrimp
comments.body: Did this with a crock of sauerkraut once. The kitchen smelled like a decision had been made. Glad Gertrude pulled through, the spite batches are always the best ones.

replies.author: gluten_full
replies.body: Spite is an underrated leavening agent. It's not in any of the books, but every baker knows.

comments.author: codfather
comments.body: my nan kept her bread dough in the oven with the light on for fifty years and never once preheated with it inside. she also never let a single one of us near that oven, and now I understand why

comments.author: elbows_up
comments.body: a warped lid, a bad attitude, and she still showed up to work. gertrude is a beer league veteran now

drip.author: petty_officer_mittens
drip.title: The floor vent has resumed operations after a long summer of disrespect. I have taken up my post and will not be moving until spring.
drip.body:
0645: warm air detected. 0646: position secured.

The small humans placed a sock on the vent "to dry it." The sock has been removed by me, personally, and filed under the couch. The large human says I am "blocking the airflow." I am the airflow now.

comments.author: gluten_full
comments.body: you and Gertrude both believe the warmest spot in the house is a birthright. neither of you is wrong

comments.author: SaveStateSteve
comments.body: you found the save point. heal to full, never leave

comments.author: twelve_rescues_later
comments.body: One vent, three cats, and a rotation schedule none of them agreed to. The oldest one works a double every night.

replies.author: petty_officer_mittens
replies.body: seniority is the only fair system. please tell the oldest one she may file grievances with me at any time

comments.author: parallel_parker
comments.body: my buddy's dog found the vent this week too. he fits on it the way a couch fits on a skateboard

comments.author: streetcar_named_delay
comments.body: The vent is the only seat in the house that runs on a reliable schedule, and you've claimed it. The TTC could learn a great deal from you.

drip.author: prairiedialup
drip.title: went to the fall supper at the community hall. you do not choose your pie. the pie lady chooses your pie.
drip.body:
asked for saskatoon berry. she looked at me for maybe two seconds and put down pumpkin. said "you'll like this better." i did like it better. she knows something about me i don't.

guy behind me asked for apple and got a short talk about his choices. then he got apple. nobody knows the criteria. nobody asks.

comments.author: FocalPointFran
comments.body: Every wedding I've ever shot has one of her running the dessert table. You don't approach. You wait to be chosen.

comments.author: portage_and_main
comments.body: Fall suppers are the best thing about the prairies, full stop. And the pie lady is never wrong. In Manitoba we just call her the authority.

replies.author: prairiedialup
replies.body: the authority. yes. no title, no election, more power than the town council

comments.author: petty_officer_mittens
comments.body: a human who hands out food based on her own private judgement and refuses to explain herself. she is a cat. you should all be very proud of her

comments.author: codfather
comments.body: there was a woman like that running the Lions Club supper back home. took one look at me and said "you're a pease pudding man." I didn't know. I was.

comments.author: SaveStateSteve
comments.body: she's an NPC with hidden stats and she can see yours

drip.author: elbows_up
drip.title: Update on our shinny goalie and the lawn chair: summer's over, so he's switched to fall furniture
drip.body:
Folding stadium seat with a back on it. Plaid wool blanket. A thermos. Between goals, and there were a lot of goals, he pours himself a tea and gazes out over the ice like he's watching the leaves turn at the cottage.

We lost 9-4 tonight. He'd like everyone to know the tea is not the reason. The blanket, he admits, might be.

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: Beer league D-man here. Don't let him blame the blanket. Our goalie eats a plain hot dog at intermission and we still gave up seven last week. It's never the snack, it's the defence. Which is me.

comments.author: codfather
comments.body: a thermos between goals is the most civilized thing that has ever happened to hockey

comments.author: streetcar_named_delay
comments.body: Act one: lawn chair. Act two: plaid blanket. I am begging for an act three with a space heater.

replies.author: elbows_up
replies.body: he's already asked whether the rink has an outlet near the bench. we're one extension cord away from a trilogy

comments.author: half_marathon_harold
comments.body: tea and a blanket is my exact post-long-run recovery routine, so I understand him completely. I also understand the nine goals

comments.author: parallel_parker
comments.body: the fact that he "admits" the blanket might be the problem means there have been meetings

late_comments.author: parallel_parker
late_comments.body: came looking for this thread after a goose stood between me and my car door in a parking lot for ten minutes this morning. they're flying south soon and they are clearly settling accounts before they go

late_comments.author: streetcar_named_delay
late_comments.body: Found my way back to this thread because the Halloween costumes are already out in stores, and I need that hotdog to know he set the standard for the entire season.

late_comments.author: SaveStateSteve
late_comments.body: back on this thread because my mom has moved on from bird feeder videos to a sourdough starter. the daily updates have begun. her captions are somehow worse
